The National Environmental Protection Agency has hit the ground running with our first major crackdown on the illegal wildlife trade.

Shoutout to our environmental crime team who disrupted a Sydney wildlife trafficking ring.

In a joint operation with Australian Federal Police and NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water they recovered:
·      36 reptiles including snakes and lizards
·      Silver and gold bullion and cash worth $300,000

The reptiles have been saved from the cruel international wildlife trade.

The individuals involved will face the full force of the law.

The National EPA is targeting wildlife crime as a compliance priority.
 
This work includes exchanging intelligence, undertaking joint investigations and using the latest technologies to detect smuggled wildlife.

We’re working with our domestic and international partners to dismantle wildlife trafficking networks and to remove the financial gains made from this crime.

We will not stop until we shut down this cruel illegal trade.
